correctness.rationale: For every planar convex body, differentiating the established first-moment Steiner polynomial gives \(q(t)^2G\prime(t)=A(L+2\pi t)(H-G)+\pi t(2A+Lt)(S-H)\). The coefficient ratio increases strictly from zero to infinity, so there is at most one isolated positive stationary radius, with the necessary collinear exterior-center condition. Sine concavity excludes non-equilateral triangle reversals. For arbitrary unequal trapezoid bases, explicit integral formulas give \(H=G\) at \(h=h_0\) but \(H>S\) strictly there; the latter follows from \(\arcsin z/z<\pi/3\) for \(0<z<1/2\). Continuity gives an open one-sided reversing-height interval and Taylor expansion the exact positive linear radius onset. Rational bounds on \(\pi\) and \(\arctan(1/3)\) certify the strict four-vertex example. The standalone checker performs 256 finite independent moment, root and sign checks; the all-parameter proof is analytic.
